jobs.description:
Zipliens is a leading lien resolution company that specializes in streamlining the lien process for personal injury law firms. We are looking for proactive, results-driven individuals to join our dynamic team.

Zipliens has grown through referrals and relationships. Now we're building a content engine that earns attention beyond them. As our Senior Content Specialist, you'll be an early member of a small, growing marketing team, reporting to the Director of Marketing and working side by side with product marketing, events, marketing operations, and design.

You'll drive how Zipliens shows up in search engines (SERPs and AI platforms) and in the resources law firms rely on: our SEO strategy and baseline, website content, the LinkedIn content calendar, blog posts, customer newsletters, and case studies. Lien resolution is technical (Medicare, Medicaid, ERISA, medical liens, subrogation), and your job is to turn that complexity into content that paralegals, case managers, and attorneys actually find, use, and trust.

You'll thrive here if you love both the craft of a sharp draft and the discipline of keyword research and performance data, enjoy pulling insight out of subject-matter experts, solving industry pain points through creative mediums, and want to build a content program from the ground up. The role is primarily hands-on writing and execution, with growing ownership of strategy and planning as the program grows.

Requirements

Responsibilities:

Build the SEO and content strategy

  • Establish an organic search baseline (traffic, impressions, rankings, branded vs. non-branded performance, top landing pages, backlinks, and technical health) before optimizing.
  • Partner with internal subject matter experts (SMEs) to develop and execute the keyword and topic strategy across lien resolution, Medicare, Medicaid, ERISA, medical liens, subrogation, settlement administration, and personal injury firm operations, balancing high-intent commercial terms with educational and long-tail searches.
  • Build and maintain the editorial/blog calendar, aligned to our ideal customer profile, product launches, and events.
  • Partner with marketing operations to connect organic visibility to qualified traffic, leads, and pipeline rather than traffic volume alone.

Create content that earns trust

  • Write and edit blog posts, guides, checklists, templates, FAQs, and reports that help personal injury law firm teams solve real lien resolution problems.
  • Partner with lien resolution SMEs, Customer Success, and company leadership to turn operational and regulatory knowledge into accurate, practical content.
  • Use Voice of the Customer (VOC) insights to develop customer case studies and spotlights that put proof behind our positioning, working with Product Marketing and Customer Success.
  • Support executive and employee thought leadership, including LinkedIn posts, bylines, and speaking abstracts.
  • Turn each strong source asset into multiple formats across channels.

Own website content and marketing collateral

  • Manage Zipliens’ public-facing resource center, partnering with subject matter experts to develop and publish content such as eBooks, whitepapers, case studies, infographics, etc.
  • Write and optimize website content, including service pages, landing pages, and metadata, in partnership with Product Marketing and Design.
  • Run on-page SEO/AEO and regular content refreshes, updating or consolidating underperforming pages.
  • Partner with marketing operations on calls to action, forms, and conversion paths so content connects to Sales.

Run channels and customer communications

  • Manage the LinkedIn content calendar, balancing core themes/pillars: thought leadership, brand awareness, campaign messaging, customer outcomes, employee advocacy, and event promotion.
  • Write and edit customer newsletter, nurture, and release-announcement copy, partnering with Customer Success, Product Marketing, and the team member building campaigns in HubSpot.
  • Create event content with the Events Manager, including pre-event promotion, session and speaker content, and post-event recaps.
  • Report on content performance regularly and recommend what to scale, update, or stop.

Qualifications:

Required

  • 5+ years in content marketing, SEO, or B2B content strategy, with a portfolio of published work.
  • Experience supporting organic traffic growth through SEO-driven content, and a solid understanding of how SEO strategy translates into rankings and conversions.
  • Excellent writing and editing skills, with the ability to translate technical or regulated topics into clear, accurate content.
  • Experience interviewing subject-matter experts and turning their input into finished content.
  • Comfortable using AI tools to speed up research, drafting, and repurposing while maintaining accuracy and brand voice.
  • Ability to work independently, manage multiple projects, and build process in a small team.
  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Journalism, English, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

Preferred

  • Hands-on experience with SEO and analytics tools (e.g., Google Search Console, GA4, Semrush, or Ahrefs) and a CMS.
  • Experience in legal, legal tech, insurance, healthcare, or other complex or regulated B2B topics; familiarity with personal injury or lien resolution is a plus.
  • Experience with HubSpot (CMS, email, and reporting).
  • Ability to travel occasionally (up to 10%) for team meetings, offsites, and select events.

jobs.title: Digital Literacy Manager / Gestionnaire en litteracie numerique
jobs.excerpt: Who we areSince 2013, Digital Moment has led digital education for Canadian youth, expanding the reach and impact of our foundational programs each year.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Since 2013, Digital Moment has led digital education for Canadian youth, expanding the reach and impact of our foundational programs each year.

But we don’t stop there—we innovate to equip youth with the skills to harness emerging technologies and tackle pressing societal challenges.

We are shaping AI-fluent leaders for a future-ready Canada with our innovative programs and initiatives.

We are driven by innovation, inclusion, and impact, empowering the next generation to shape technology for good. Working with us means making a difference every day by equipping youth with essential digital skills to navigate a technology-driven world.

We are a fully-remote, small and mighty, team that embraces innovation, challenges the status quo and experiments with new ideas to drive meaningful change. We’ve built a culture that is positive, collaborative and focused on the purpose we want to create.

We’re currently looking for a Digital Literacy Lead to manage our team of Digital Literacy Educators and our initiatives in formal education.

(French version below)

Here’s an overview of the Position

We’re seeking a strategic, execution-oriented Manager to lead our national team of Regional Outreach & Digital Literacy Educators. In this role, you will design, execute, and oversee the operational strategy for how Digital Moment engages K-12 education systems across Canada, promotes our national AI Literacy Framework, and scales educator professional learning across all provinces.

Our organizational culture is highly collaborative and hands-on—everyone at Digital Moment rolls up their sleeves to get the work done. While you will be responsible for setting strategy, establishing KPIs, and keeping your team on track, you will also lead from the front by actively jumping into outreach meetings, pitching to major education stakeholders, and delivering educator training sessions alongside your team.

Key Responsibilities

Outreach Strategy & Campaign Design

  • Design and implement the national roadmap for stakeholder outreach, framework promotion, and educator training delivery across Western Canada, Ontario, Quebec, and Eastern Canada.
  • Establish regional engagement targets, outreach priorities, and operational campaign plans to systematically reach school boards, ministries, and educational associations.
  • Define national adoption goals, engagement targets, and key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure reach, workshop delivery, and partnership progress.
  • Work with leadership to align regional outreach strategies with broader organizational goals and funding commitments.

Team Leadership, Coaching & Operational Performance

  • Lead, manage, and mentor a distributed team of Regional Educators, ensuring they have the tools, guidance, and support needed to succeed in their territories.
  • Establish regular reporting cadences and maintain tracking systems to monitor team performance, outreach pipelines, completed activities, barriers, and upcoming actions.
  • Provide hands-on coaching to help Regional Educators navigate complex stakeholder environments, close partnership agreements, and optimize workshop delivery.
  • Ensure consistency and quality in training delivery, framework representation, and partner communication across all regions.

Hands-On Engagement & Strategic Partnerships (Leading by Example)

  • Directly manage key strategic accounts, high-level ministry interactions, and major national/provincial partnerships.
  • Actively step in to conduct outreach meetings, pitch Digital Moment’s AI Literacy Framework, and facilitate professional development sessions/webinars alongside Regional Educators.
  • Maintain direct involvement in field activities to stay grounded in educator needs, regional nuances, and market dynamics.
  • Support the drafting and execution of high-level Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs), partnership agreements, and joint implementation plans.

Monitoring, Reporting & Strategic Insights

  • Synthesize engagement metrics, training data, participant feedback, and field insights from across the country to track overall progress and continuous improvement.
  • Provide regular, comprehensive updates to executive leadership regarding team performance against KPIs, emerging regional opportunities, system barriers, and strategic recommendations.
  • Translate field intelligence into actionable recommendations for internal teams to refine our AI Literacy Framework, professional learning content, and knowledge mobilization materials.

Ideal Candidate Profile

  • 5+ years of leadership experience in K-12 education, educational non-profits, or edtech, with a proven track record of managing distributed regional teams.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, and monitoring multi-region outreach strategies, training rollouts, or partnership pipelines.
  • Extensive hands-on experience in K-12 educator engagement, including workshop facilitation, stakeholder pitching, and relationship management.
  • Experience leading partnership development processes, including high-level memoranda of understanding (MoUs), joint workplans, and complex stakeholder agreements.
  • Experience tracking organizational outcomes, managing performance against KPIs, and reporting progress to senior leadership or boards.
  • Comprehensive understanding of Canadian K-12 education systems, provincial curricula, governance structures, and decision-making processes across multiple provinces.
  • Deep knowledge of AI literacy, digital technology integration, and emerging trends in K-12 education.
  • Strong grasp of educational change management and how to scale initiatives across diverse provincial contexts.
  • Exceptional leadership, team management, and coaching abilities for distributed environments.
  • Outstanding verbal, written, and presentation skills; comfortable acting as a key spokesperson for Digital Moment across regional and national forums.
  • Strong strategic planning, project management, and analytical skills to organize national outreach campaigns and track team KPIs.
  • Ability to translate high-level organizational strategy into clear, executable workplans for regional leads.
  • "Lead from the front" mindset—enthusiastic about rolling up your sleeves to deliver workshops, conduct outreach pitches, and directly support team members in the field.
  • Mission-driven with a deep passion for scaling ethical, accessible AI literacy in K-12 education.
  • Agile, proactive, and resilient when navigating complex organizational structures and emerging opportunities.
  • Highly collaborative with strong diplomacy, emotional intelligence, and relationship-building capabilities.
  • Bilingualism (English/French) is a strong asset.

If this sounds like you - we want to hear from you!

Here’s what we offer our employees:

  • Fully remote work
  • Competitive salary
  • Generous time off policy (10 wellness days and 20 days of vacation annually)
  • Health benefits: benefits coverage as of Day 1
  • Matching RRSP contribution program

Qui nous sommes

Depuis 2013, Digital Moment est un chef de file en matière d’éducation au numérique auprès des jeunes canadiens. Chaque année, nous élargissons la portée et renforçons l’impact de nos programmes fondamentaux.

Mais nous ne nous arrêtons pas là : nous innovons constamment afin de donner aux jeunes les compétences nécessaires pour tirer parti des technologies émergentes et relever les grands défis de société.

Grâce à nos programmes et initiatives novateurs, nous formons des leaders maîtrisant l’intelligence artificielle (IA), capables de contribuer à un Canada prêt à relever les défis de demain.

Portés par l’innovation, l’inclusion et l’impact, nous donnons à la prochaine génération les moyens de mettre la technologie au service du bien commun. Travailler avec nous, c’est faire une différence chaque jour en aidant les jeunes à acquérir les compétences numériques essentielles pour évoluer dans un monde façonné par la technologie.

Notre petite équipe, entièrement en télétravail, est dynamique et ambitieuse. Nous accueillons l’innovation, remettons en question le statu quo et expérimentons de nouvelles idées pour susciter des changements concrets et significatifs. Nous avons bâti une culture positive et collaborative, axée sur la mission que nous souhaitons accomplir.

Nous sommes actuellement à la recherche d’une personne responsable de la littératie numérique pour encadrer notre équipe de spécialistes en éducation à la littératie numérique et superviser nos initiatives en milieu scolaire.

Aperçu du poste

Nous recherchons une personne gestionnaire stratégique et axée sur l’exécution pour diriger notre équipe pancanadienne de spécialistes régionaux en mobilisation et en littératie numérique. Dans le cadre de ce poste, vous concevrez, mettrez en œuvre et superviserez la stratégie opérationnelle visant à mobiliser les systèmes d’éducation de la maternelle à la 12e année partout au Canada, à promouvoir notre Cadre national de littératie en IA et à déployer à plus grande échelle les activités de perfectionnement professionnel du personnel enseignant dans toutes les provinces.

Notre culture organisationnelle repose sur une forte collaboration et une approche pratique : chez Digital Moment, tout le monde met la main à la pâte pour faire avancer les choses. Bien que vous soyez responsable de définir la stratégie, d’établir les indicateurs clés de performance (ICP) et de veiller à ce que votre équipe atteigne ses objectifs, vous devrez également montrer l’exemple en participant activement aux rencontres de mobilisation, en présentant nos initiatives aux principaux acteurs du milieu de l’éducation et en animant des formations pour le personnel enseignant aux côtés de votre équipe.

Principales responsabilités

Stratégie de mobilisation et conception de campagnes

  • Concevoir et mettre en œuvre la feuille de route nationale pour la mobilisation des parties prenantes, la promotion du cadre et la prestation de formations au personnel enseignant dans l’Ouest canadien, en Ontario, au Québec et dans l’Est du Canada.
  • Établir des objectifs régionaux de mobilisation, définir les priorités de sensibilisation et élaborer des plans de campagne opérationnels afin de joindre systématiquement les conseils scolaires, les ministères et les associations du milieu de l’éducation.
  • Définir les objectifs nationaux d’adoption, les cibles de mobilisation et les indicateurs clés de performance (ICP) permettant de mesurer la portée des initiatives, la prestation des ateliers et l’avancement des partenariats.
  • Collaborer avec la direction afin d’harmoniser les stratégies régionales de mobilisation avec les objectifs organisationnels globaux et les engagements liés au financement.

Leadership d’équipe, accompagnement et performance opérationnelle

  • Diriger, encadrer et accompagner une équipe répartie de spécialistes régionaux en éducation, en veillant à ce que chaque personne dispose des outils, des conseils et du soutien nécessaires pour réussir dans son territoire.
  • Mettre en place des mécanismes de suivi et de reddition de comptes réguliers ainsi que des systèmes de suivi permettant de surveiller la performance de l’équipe, les démarches de mobilisation en cours, les activités réalisées, les obstacles rencontrés et les prochaines étapes.
  • Offrir un accompagnement pratique aux spécialistes régionaux afin de les aider à composer avec des environnements complexes, à conclure des ententes de partenariat et à optimiser la prestation des ateliers.
  • Assurer la cohérence et la qualité des formations, de la présentation du cadre et des communications avec les partenaires dans toutes les régions.

Mobilisation directe et partenariats stratégiques : montrer l’exemple

  • Gérer directement les comptes stratégiques clés, les relations de haut niveau avec les ministères et les principaux partenariats nationaux et provinciaux.
  • Participer activement aux rencontres de mobilisation, présenter le Cadre de littératie en IA de Digital Moment et animer des séances et des webinaires de perfectionnement professionnel aux côtés des spécialistes régionaux.
  • Rester directement impliqué dans les activités sur le terrain afin de bien comprendre les besoins du personnel enseignant, les particularités régionales et les réalités du milieu.
  • Contribuer à la rédaction et à la mise en œuvre de protocoles d’entente de haut niveau, d’accords de partenariat et de plans conjoints de mise en œuvre.

Suivi, reddition de comptes et réflexion stratégique

  • Synthétiser les indicateurs de mobilisation, les données sur les formations, les commentaires des participantes et participants ainsi que les observations recueillies sur le terrain partout au pays afin de suivre les progrès globaux et de favoriser l’amélioration continue.
  • Présenter régulièrement à la haute direction des bilans détaillés sur la performance de l’équipe par rapport aux ICP, les nouvelles possibilités régionales, les obstacles systémiques et les recommandations stratégiques.
  • Transformer les informations recueillies sur le terrain en recommandations concrètes destinées aux équipes internes afin d’améliorer notre Cadre de littératie en IA, nos contenus de perfectionnement professionnel et nos outils de mobilisation et de transfert des connaissances.

Profil de la personne recherchée

  • Posséder au moins cinq ans d’expérience en leadership dans le secteur de l’éducation de la maternelle à la 12e année, au sein d’organismes sans but lucratif en éducation ou dans le domaine des technologies éducatives, et avoir fait ses preuves dans la gestion d’équipes régionales réparties géographiquement.
  • Avoir une expérience démontrée dans la conception, la mise en œuvre et le suivi de stratégies de mobilisation multirégionales, de déploiements de formations ou de démarches de développement de partenariats.
  • Posséder une vaste expérience pratique de la mobilisation du personnel enseignant de la maternelle à la 12e année, notamment en animation d’ateliers, en présentation de propositions aux parties prenantes et en gestion de relations.
  • Avoir de l’expérience dans la conduite de processus de développement de partenariats, y compris la négociation de protocoles d’entente de haut niveau, l’élaboration de plans de travail conjoints et la gestion d’accords complexes entre différentes parties prenantes.
  • Avoir de l’expérience dans le suivi des résultats organisationnels, la gestion de la performance en fonction d’ICP et la présentation de bilans à la haute direction ou à des conseils d’administration.
  • Posséder une compréhension approfondie des systèmes d’éducation canadiens de la maternelle à la 12e année, des programmes d’études provinciaux, des structures de gouvernance et des processus décisionnels dans plusieurs provinces.
  • Avoir une connaissance approfondie de la littératie en IA, de l’intégration des technologies numériques et des tendances émergentes en éducation de la maternelle à la 12e année.
  • Bien comprendre la gestion du changement en éducation et les moyens de déployer des initiatives à grande échelle dans des contextes provinciaux diversifiés.
  • Démontrer d’excellentes aptitudes en leadership, en gestion d’équipe et en accompagnement dans un environnement de travail réparti.
  • Posséder d’excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite ainsi qu’en présentation, et être à l’aise d’agir comme porte-parole de Digital Moment lors d’événements régionaux et nationaux.
  • Faire preuve de solides compétences en planification stratégique, en gestion de projet et en analyse afin d’organiser des campagnes nationales de mobilisation et de suivre les ICP de l’équipe.
  • Être capable de traduire une stratégie organisationnelle globale en plans de travail clairs et réalisables pour les responsables régionaux.
  • Adopter une approche de leadership exemplaire et participative, en étant enthousiaste à l’idée de mettre la main à la pâte pour animer des ateliers, mener des démarches de mobilisation et soutenir directement les membres de l’équipe sur le terrain.
  • Être profondément motivé par notre mission et passionné par le déploiement à grande échelle d’une littératie en IA éthique et accessible dans le système d’éducation de la maternelle à la 12e année.
  • Faire preuve d’agilité, de proactivité et de résilience pour évoluer dans des structures organisationnelles complexes et saisir de nouvelles occasions.
  • Être une personne très collaborative, dotée d’un grand sens de la diplomatie, d’une excellente intelligence émotionnelle et de solides aptitudes à établir et à entretenir des relations.
  • La maîtrise du français et de l’anglais constitue un atout important.

Si cette description vous correspond, nous voulons vous rencontrer!

Ce que nous offrons à notre personnel

The Enterprise CSM will own executive relationships with program stakeholders and partner organizations while leading and mentoring a team of In-State Customer Success Managers responsible for provider engagement and frontline program support. This role requires strong leadership, program management, and the ability to drive measurable outcomes across complex healthcare and government environments.

What You'll Do

Enterprise Program Leadership
  • Serve as the primary strategic owner of programming within the state, ensuring program success across participating providers
  • Manage relationships with stakeholders across multiple levels — agency leadership, executive sponsors, program administrators, provider executives, and clinical leaders
  • Own full-stack customer success support across software, hardware, and services for the enterprise program
  • Lead large-scale program deployments and implementations, including:
    • Program planning and coordination
    • Cross-functional collaboration with Product, Engineering, and Operations
    • Platform configuration and readiness
    • Quality assurance (QA)
    • Go-live execution and post-implementation optimization
  • Drive enterprise adoption and outcomes across the provider network
  • Deliver executive-level communications including Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), performance reporting, and program updates
  • Partner closely with Product and Engineering to represent enterprise customer needs, capture feedback, and influence roadmap priorities
  • Ensure strong program performance across key success metrics including adoption, program health, satisfaction, and measurable ROI
Team Leadership & People Management
  • Lead and manage a team of 1–3 In-State Customer Success Managers supporting providers across the state
  • Serve as the first point of escalation for customer issues and help resolve complex provider challenges
  • Partner with leadership on recruiting and hiring activities, including job description development, interview planning, and candidate evaluation
  • Onboard and train new In-State Customer Success Managers, maintaining and improving onboarding guides and enablement materials
  • Support the growth and development of team members through regular 1:1s, performance reviews, individual development plans, and coaching
  • Contribute to building a scalable Customer Experience organization capable of supporting continued enterprise and government program growth
Strategic Growth & Program Development
  • Act as the internal program leader for providers in the state, ensuring alignment between customer needs and company strategic goals
  • Identify and implement operational improvements that scale the customer experience as enterprise programs expand
  • Lead and support upsells and expansion opportunities within the enterprise program
  • Document customer insights, feature requests, and program feedback to inform product development and roadmap planning
  • Represent Customer Success in cross-functional initiatives and executive-level strategic discussions

How We Measure Success

What Success Looks Like
  • Deep Partnership: You have developed a meaningful, trusting relationship with program stakeholders. They view the company not just as a vendor, but as a critical strategic partner in their mission to improve resident safety and program accountability.
  • Operational Harmony: The "State Model" for software deployment is seen as a gold standard within the company — high adoption rates, minimal deployment friction, measurable ROI for providers.
  • Team Excellence: You have built a high-performing In-State CSM team that feels supported, coached, and empowered to navigate the unique challenges of frontline healthcare environments.
  • Program Expansion: Your leadership has secured the program's longevity through high renewal rates and identification of new opportunities to expand impact within the state's healthcare ecosystem.

What We're Looking For

Required
  • 7+ years of experience in Customer Success, Enterprise Account Management, or a similar customer-facing role — preferably within healthcare SaaS
  • Demonstrated success managing large enterprise or government accounts with complex stakeholder environments
  • Direct people management experience — leading, hiring, onboarding, and developing customer success or account management teams
  • Strong program and project management skills with experience delivering multi-site implementations
  • Excellent communication skills with executive presence and experience engaging C-suite and public sector stakeholders

About this role:

Our Business Development teams play a critical role in expanding Gartner’s presence across the global market. Gartner Business Development Executives strategically acquire new clients by cultivating trust-based relationships with C-level executives to understand their mission critical priorities, then uncovering opportunities to deliver client-value through the lens of the industry in which they operate. Gartner Business Developers own and drive the full sales cycle, from identifying prospects to closure. They then transition new clients to the account management team for ongoing value delivery.

Our Business Development teams are relentless about building trust-based, value add relationships with clients, delivering long-term client value, and building their book of business over time. Business developers are results driven, client committed, and highly collaborative.

Business Developers will be given a territory of Large Enterprise prospects, which may be completely new prospects with no existing spend or could be clients within other Gartner areas. In our GBS Large Enterprise segment, Business Developers work with prospects with +$1bil in annual revenue.

What you will do:

  • Seek out and drive new business opportunities with new-to-Gartner organizations across your territory, from initial client outreach to close, targeting Large Enterprise organizations.

  • Convert viable prospects into active Gartner clients, owning the full sales conversation and negotiation, through to the transition of new clients to the account management team.

  • Continually build a pipeline of high-quality opportunities to deliver against your sales metrics ensuring KPI’s are met.

  • Align the right combination of insight, guidance, and practical tools to bring value to the partnership.

  • Quota responsibility for your assigned territory.

  • Manage complex high-revenue sales across matrix and diverse business environments.

  • Own forecasting and account planning on a monthly/quarterly/annual basis.

What you will need:

  • 5+ years’ B2B sales experience, preferably within complex, intangible sales environments.

  • Business development or new-client acquisition experience in a selling role highly desired.

  • Experience selling to and/or influencing C-Level Executives.

  • Proven track record meeting and exceeding sales targets.

  • Proven ability to precisely manage and forecast a complex sale process.

  • Willingness to conduct travel as needed.

  • Bachelor's degree desired

Progression within Business Development Executive Roles:

Gartner offers a lifetime of opportunities driven by our growth. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

Gartner has a promote from within culture and limitless opportunities for progression. Gartner leaders embrace this culture and are focused on helping associates achieve success in current role, as well as coaching associates to the next role or path, whether it be more senior BD levels, account management paths, or sales leadership.

Typical internal promotions include:

  • Business Development Director

  • Team Lead

  • Sales Manager

Most of our Sales Managers and Team Leads are hired internally as part of our progression path.

What you will get:

  • Competitive salary, generous paid time off policy, charity match program, and more!

  • Uncapped commission structure

  • World-class sales training programs and skill development programs

  • Annual "Winners Circle" event attendance at exclusive destinations for top performers

  • Collaborative, team-oriented culture that embraces inclusion

  • Professional development and career growth opportunities

Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

Gartner believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is 102,000 USD - 147,000 USD. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range, or be above or below the range, based on factors including, but not limited to, education, training, experience, professional achievement, business need, and location. In addition to base salary, employees will participate in either an annual bonus plan based on company and individual performance, or a role-based, uncapped sales incentive plan. Our talent acquisition team will provide the specific opportunity on our bonus or incentive programs to eligible candidates. We also offer market leading benefit programs including generous PTO, a 401k match up to $7,200 per year, the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount, and more.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Precision Medicine Executive, Rare Blood Disease Tri-State

Location: Remote, US


About the Job:

The Precision Medicine Executive, Rare Blood Disease is a field-based commercial role focused on encouraging diagnostic testing and enhancing patient identification for systemic mastocytosis and future precision medicine therapies within Sanofi’s portfolio. This individual will partner with key accounts, diagnostic laboratories, and cross-functional Sanofi teams to support disease education, testing adoption, and account-level execution aligned to business and patient needs.

Join the team transforming care for people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and neurological conditions. In Specialty Care, you'll help deliver breakthrough treatments that bring hope to patients with some of the highest unmet needs.

About Sanofi

We're an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people's lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people's lives.


Main responsibilities


  • Build relationships with key account stakeholders, including pathology, laboratory, clinical, and executive decision-makers, to support appropriate diagnostic testing and patient identification.
  • Develop and execute account plans that advance high-quality diagnostic, biomarker, and genomic testing aligned to Rare Blood Disease priorities.
  • Educate stakeholders on systemic mastocytosis, diagnostic pathways, and the role of precision medicine in patient care.
  • Partner with commercial, medical, marketing, access, and field teams to deliver approved education, resources, and account-level initiatives.
  • Identify and communicate customer needs, market insights, diagnostic barriers, and opportunities to improve testing pathways.
  • Serve as a regional subject matter expert for diagnostics and precision medicine in systemic mastocytosis and future applicable therapies.
  • Represent Sanofi at relevant local, regional, and national congresses and customer-facing forums in accordance with company policies.
  • Maintain compliance with all applicable regulatory requirements, healthcare laws, Sanofi Code of Conduct, and EBI Guidance

About You

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree
  • 5+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical, healthcare, biotechnology, or related life sciences industries and in diagnostics or precision medicine
  • Ability to travel regularly within the assigned geography.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in life sciences, medicine, pharmacy, business, or a related field.
  • Background in pathology, molecular biology, diagnostics, hematology, oncology, rare disease, or precision medicine.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, and planning skills with the ability to work effectively in a field-based, cross-functional environment.
  • Working knowledge of diagnostic testing, biomarker or genomic testing, and patient identification pathways.
  • Experience engaging external healthcare stakeholders and account decision-makers in complex clinical or laboratory environments.
  • Experience supporting specialty product launches, indication expansions, diagnostic strategy, or market development.
  • Understanding of diagnostic market dynamics, including reimbursement, regulatory, policy, provider, patient, and payer considerations.
  • Ability to influence without authority, build credibility, align stakeholders, and drive adoption of new approaches or technologies.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills with a patient-focused and compliance-oriented mindset.

Why choose us?

  • Bring the miracles of science to life alongside a supportive, future-focused team.​​
  • Discover endless opportunities to grow your talent and drive your career, whether it’s through a promotion or lateral move, at home or internationally.​​
  • Enjoy a thoughtful, well-crafted rewards package that recognizes your contribution and amplifies your impact.​​
  • Take good care of yourself and your family, with a wide range of health and wellbeing benefits including high-quality healthcare, prevention and wellness programs and at least 14 weeks’ gender-neutral parental leave.​

jobs.description:
Suralink® is the agentic automation platform for accounting professionals and their clients, leading the global charge in AI-driven accounting technology. As the leading AI platform for accounting firms, Suralink serves more than 50% of the top 100 enterprise accounting firms in the United States and has over 800,000 users globally.

Our mission is to empower the people we serve to redefine the meaning of efficiency in the accounting technology industry. Our award-winning SaaS platform was built for CPA firms, providing a simple, secure way to manage audit, tax, and advisory engagements.

Recognized for growth, innovation, and culture, we foster a highly collaborative, remote-first environment where exceptional, motivated professionals can make a meaningful impact. If you're passionate about building relationships and driving growth at a fast-growing SaaS company, we'd love to talk with you

Who we are looking for:

We are looking for a HubSpot-focused Marketing Operations Specialist to help run the systems, data, and reporting behind our demand generation and pipeline. Day to day, you will build and maintain workflows, lists, and campaign operations in HubSpot, keep our data clean, and produce the reporting Marketing relies on. This role is a good fit for someone with a solid HubSpot foundation who wants to build their skills in marketing operations and take on more strategic work over time.

Reporting directly to the Revenue Operations Manager, you will work closely with Marketing, learn how our revenue systems fit together, and take on more ownership as you grow in the role.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain HubSpot workflows, lists, forms, properties, and campaign assets, following our established standards and naming conventions

  • Support campaign and webinar operations end to end, including list builds, registration and follow-up workflows, and post-event data cleanup

  • Support lead management and lifecycle stage processes, and troubleshoot routing and lifecycle issues as they come up, escalating changes to routing rules or lifecycle definitions to the Revenue Operations Manager

  • Apply and QA our attribution and UTM standards so source data stays accurate and reportable

  • Support Marketing with CRM administration, including property requests, pipeline and deal stage hygiene, and user issues, in partnership with the Revenue Operations Manager

  • Monitor integrations between HubSpot and our marketing tech stack, and flag and help resolve data sync issues

  • Run regular data quality audits covering duplicates, enrichment gaps, standardization, and imports

  • Build and maintain HubSpot reports and dashboards for funnel, campaign, and pipeline performance, and flag trends or anomalies to the team

  • Document processes and system configurations, and help train Marketing users on new features and process changes

Experience and Professional Qualifications:

  • 2+ years in marketing operations, including hands-on HubSpot experience building workflows, lists, properties, and reports

  • Working experience building HubSpot workflows, lists, properties, and reports

  • Strong attention to detail and a habit of checking your own work

  • Comfortable in spreadsheets and with basic data work such as pivot tables, lookups, and cleaning and importing data

  • Clear written and verbal communication, including documenting processes and explaining your work to non-technical teammates

Additional Preferred Qualifications:

  • HubSpot Academy certifications, such as Marketing Hub Software or Reporting

  • Experience in a B2B SaaS environment

  • Exposure to HubSpot custom objects, integrations, or data enrichment tools

  • Exposure to attribution, funnel reporting, or UTM tracking

  • Interest in BI tools, SQL, or AI tools that make operational work faster

Competencies

  • Systems and Automation Orientation:Looks for ways to make repetitive work faster and more reliable through automation and better process.

  • Attention to Detail:Holds a high bar for data accuracy and consistency, and catches issues before they reach a report.

  • Analytical Thinking:Uses data to answer questions, checks whether the numbers make sense, and can explain what a report shows.

  • Communication:Explains their work clearly, keeps stakeholders updated on requests, and raises problems early.

  • Ownership:Follows through on commitments, sees work through from request to finished result, and asks for help when stuck.

  • Curiosity and Coachability:Asks good questions, learns quickly, and uses feedback to get better.

At Suralink, our values guide everything we do:

  • Customer Obsessed: We seek to understand those we serve deeply and are committed to serving them better than anyone else.

  • Passionately Motivated: We care about what we do, which drives us to work hard, show grit, and go above and beyond to achieve great outcomes.

  • Constantly Improving: We are eager to learn and grow. Challenges are opportunities to innovate and enhance our solutions.

  • Team Focused: We know that our success is built together. We support one another and celebrate team achievements.

  • Highly Reliable: We demonstrate good judgment, honor our commitments, and are accountable for our results.

Why Suralink?

There’s a lot to love about working at Suralink! Here are a few of the benefits you can expect:

  • Remote-friendly policy

  • Medical/vision/dental insurance

  • Flexible PTO policy and ten paid holidays

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development allowance

  • Community involvement

jobs.excerpt: Kampgrounds of America, Inc.  (KOA) is the world’s largest network of privately owned campgrounds and the leader in outdoor hospitality.
jobs.description:
Kampgrounds of America, Inc. (KOA) is the world’s largest network of privately owned campgrounds and the leader in outdoor hospitality. KOA has 500+ locations across the United States and Canada including a mix of franchised and company-owned parks (OAK). Founded in 1962, the mission of KOA is “connecting people to the outdoors and each other,” and those who represent the brand share the values of being family-oriented, passionate, entrepreneurial, customer-focused, and innovative. At KOA, we believe the outdoors is fun and for everyone. We are committed to having an environment where all are treated with dignity and respect. We strive to:

  • intentionally create a sense of community and belonging for our guests, employees and franchise partners
  • continually educate ourselves and expand our knowledge to foster an inclusive and supportive environment
  • sustain a culture that promotes diversity of thought and experiences
  • ensure everyone has the ability to experience the outdoors and that our facilities are accessible to all
  • drive change in our company and industry through action and implementation

Summary:

The SEO Manager manages and executes KOA's organic search and discovery programs across traditional search engines, AI-powered discovery experiences, and local search. This role supports the development of KOA's national Search Engine Optimization (SEO), Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), and multi-location/local SEO strategy and translates that strategy into measurable programs, recommendations, and improvements across KOA.com and KOA's campground network. The SEO Manager serves as KOA's primary subject-matter expert for organic search and discovery, with broad working knowledge across technical SEO, content, on-page optimization, authority/off-page signals, site performance, structured data, Google Business Profiles, local citations and profiles, and emerging AI discovery. The SEO Manager identifies visibility gaps and opportunities, develops actionable recommendations, coordinates implementation with Product, Engineering, Content, Digital Experience, Media, Analytics, franchisees, and agency partners, and measures whether those actions improve qualified visibility and business outcomes. SEO Manager also manages the day-to-day operation of KOA's local-search program, including vendor and tool relationships, profile standards, reporting, franchisee support, education, and issue escalation.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Manage and execute KOA's organic search and discovery programs across national SEO, local SEO, and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), aligning work to the broader digital, brand, consumer-growth, and discovery strategies established by Digital leadership.
  • Identify organic-search and AI-discovery opportunities and translate them into recommendations and a prioritized work plan spanning technical SEO, content, authority, local search, and digital experience improvements; distinguish meaningful opportunities from isolated requests or ranking fluctuations.
  • Manage day-to-day SEO/GEO vendor relationships and performance; coordinate scopes of work, deliverables, timelines, reporting, and performance expectations with Digital leadership, and escalate material scope, capability, or performance concerns.
  • Administer and optimize KOA's multi-location SEO and local-listing management tools, coordinate vendor support and adoption, and maintain accurate and scalable management of campground profiles and location data within approved standards.
  • Serve as KOA's subject-matter expert across the major SEO disciplines: technical SEO, on-page SEO, content optimization, off-page/authority signals, local SEO, structured data/schema, crawl/indexation, internal linking, information architecture, and search-result presentation.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering to identify and prioritize technical SEO requirements and risks, including crawlability, indexability, rendering, canonicalization, redirects, structured data, internal linking, Core Web Vitals, page speed, mobile performance, and platform migrations.
  • Partner with Content and Digital Experience teams to improve page usefulness, relevance, information architecture, templates, internal linking, metadata, content quality, and content coverage based on guest intent and search demand.
  • Develop recommendations for KOA's evolving GEO and AI-discovery approach, including entity clarity, authoritative content, structured information, citation-worthiness, content accessibility, and emerging machine-readable discovery requirements; coordinate approved improvements with relevant teams.
  • Manage implementation and ongoing operation of KOA's local-search program across the campground network, including Google Business Profile (GBP) and other local-profile governance, categories, attributes, photos, posts where appropriate, reviews/reputation signals, local landing pages, citations, directory profiles, duplicate/suppression issues, and location/entity consistency.
  • Develop and maintain standards, guidance, and scalable operating procedures with Digital leadership so franchisees and staff understand what KOA manages centrally, what campgrounds manage locally, and how issues are escalated.
  • Monitor organic and local visibility by market, location, query theme, device, and search surface; diagnose whether changes are driven by demand, ranking, competitive activity, technical issues, content gaps, local-profile signals, or changing search-result experiences.
  • Work closely with paid media and advertising teams to identify and close search-visibility gaps, coordinate paid and organic coverage, share keyword and market intelligence, and avoid treating SEO and paid search as isolated channels.
  • Partner with Analytics and Digital leadership to develop and maintain SEO/GEO/local-search reporting, dashboards, baselines, targets, and measurement methodology; connect visibility metrics to qualified traffic, reservations, revenue, engagement, and other business outcomes where attribution is supportable.
  • Prepare recurring reporting and recommendations for Digital leadership and relevant teams that explain what changed, why it changed, what KOA can influence, recommended actions, and expected outcomes.
  • Serve as the primary SEO/local-search escalation point for franchisees. Participate in franchisee calls when needed, diagnose visibility concerns using evidence, explain findings in practical language, and provide actionable recommendations.
  • Serve as the SEO SME for KOA staff supporting local and franchise marketing; create guidance, playbooks, training, office hours, and decision frameworks that allow common issues to be resolved consistently without requiring one-off intervention.
  • Monitor competitor visibility, SERP changes, AI-search developments, local-search platform changes, algorithm updates, and emerging search behaviors; communicate material implications and recommend practical adjustments to Digital leadership and relevant teams.
  • Support major KOA.com releases, migrations, redesigns, and new product capabilities with SEO requirements, pre-launch validation, launch monitoring, and post-launch analysis to protect and grow organic visibility.
  • Maintain a testing-and-learning approach: develop hypotheses, partner on SEO/CRO experiments where appropriate, document results, and use evidence to refine recommendations and program execution.
  • In-person attendance will be required on a yearly cycle to attend departmental meetings and/or staff development meetings.

Non-Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • This job description is not intended to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in marketing, business, communications, technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • 3+ years of hands-on SEO experience.
  • Strong generalist knowledge across technical SEO, on-page SEO, content strategy/optimization, off-page/authority development, local SEO, and structured data.
  • Demonstrated experience with multi-location/local SEO, including Google Business Profile management, local listings/citations, location landing pages, review/reputation signals, and duplicate/profile issue resolution.
  • Strong understanding of how site architecture, rendering, crawl/indexation, internal linking, Core Web Vitals, page speed, mobile experience, and platform changes affect organic performance.
  • Strong understanding of how content quality, topical relevance, entity clarity, authority, and user intent influence visibility across traditional and emerging AI-powered search experiences.
  • Working knowledge of GEO / AI-search optimization and a demonstrated ability to evaluate emerging search behaviors without relying on unproven tactics.
  • Experience managing SEO agencies, technology vendors, and/or multi-location SEO platforms; able to hold partners accountable while integrating their work into an internal strategy.
  • Strong analytical skills and experience using tools such as Google Search Console, GA4, Google Business Profile performance data, enterprise SEO platforms, local SEO/listing platforms, crawling tools, rank/visibility tracking, and BI/reporting environments.
  • Ability to diagnose complex visibility changes by separating search demand, rankings, SERP composition, competitive activity, technical health, content performance, and local signals.
  • Ability to communicate technical and analytical SEO concepts clearly to executives, marketers, engineers, franchisees, and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience partnering with Product, Engineering, Content, Analytics, and Paid Media teams and translating SEO findings into prioritized cross-functional action.
  • Strong organizational and vendor-management skills, with the ability to manage enterprise priorities while responding effectively to location-level escalations.

Preferred Education and Experience:

  • Hands-on SEO experience, preferably supporting a large consumer website, multi-location brand, marketplace, franchise system, travel/hospitality business, or similarly complex digital ecosystem.
  • Experience with a headless CMS and modern web architecture.
  • Experience with large-scale location or franchise websites and distributed content/profile governance.
  • Working knowledge of HTML, JavaScript rendering, HTTP status behavior, schema.org structured data, robots directives, XML sitemaps, and web performance diagnostics.
  • Experience with SEO experimentation, content testing, or conversion-rate optimization.
  • Experience analyzing visibility across AI search/answer engines and traditional search-result features.

Physical Demands and Working Conditions:

  • Work is performed in an office environment and requires the ability to operate standard office equipment and keyboard, including lifting and carrying a laptop and other small items up to 20 pounds.
  • Prolonged exposure to computer screen and artificial lighting.
  • Use of repetitive motion, standing, bending, sitting, lifting, and walking short distances.
  • May be expected to drive a vehicle to KOA locations, other locations as directed, and conferences which requires close and distance vision, sitting, seeing and reading signs, traffic signals, other vehicles, etc. Travel occurs in all weather conditions, including extreme heat and cold.
  • Frequent in person interaction with KOA employees in various settings, where noise level is typically low to moderate, including office spaces.
  • Will experience occasional interruptions and shifting priorities.

jobs.description:
About the role

We are looking for a Senior Project Manager to own our larger accounts and multi-phase programs, from signed contract through discovery, build, launch and the first months after go-live.

This is a senior delivery role. You are accountable for the budget, scope, timeline, and the customer relationship on every project you run, and you carry the conversations that come with them. We want someone who has already managed complex enterprise implementations, understands the challenges of ERP integration, and who has worked in a delivery model where AI does a meaningful share of the work. In this model, you understand that the project manager’s job is to make sure the work is defined well enough for AI and human steps to flow smoothly and with minimal intervention.

What you will do

  • Own the project from signature to post-launch and deliver it on time, in scope, and on budget.

  • Turn the contract into a work breakdown with estimates that roll up to the sold number, and close discovery with the Solution Architect on that basis.

  • Keep the backlog ready. Every piece of work has a trace to the agreed solution design, acceptance criteria, an estimate and its dependencies before it goes to the team.

  • Keep the project record complete, with every project meeting recorded and filed so the design, the plan and the team’s AI tools can work from it.

  • Run the project week to week. Record and communicate budget burn, risks and mitigations, blockers with an owner and a date, dependencies on the customer’s IT and ERP partners, and a status the sponsor can act on without a call.

  • Carry the hard conversations. When scope or expectations drift, say what it costs, defend the team’s estimate and the agreed scope, and route the rest through change control.

  • Keep the customer relationship and the team healthy through the hard parts. The sponsor and customer trust your numbers, and the team trusts you to protect their estimates and their time.

  • Take the first call on customer escalations and bring rebaselines and change orders to the customer on your own.

  • Mentor Project Managers and build the templates, dashboards and working practices the PMO runs on.

What we are looking for

Experience and qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Seven or more years managing software implementation projects with a contracted budget for enterprise customers, with commerce, PIM or ERP integration projects in the Microsoft ecosystem strongly preferred.

  • Experience delivering in an AI-accelerated methodology, where meeting records, solution design and backlog quality are what the AI tools and the engineers build from, and where you have seen what happens when they are not in order.

  • A track record of turning a Statement of Work and its change orders into a work breakdown that rolls up to the contract, and of holding that number through delivery.

  • Working knowledge of Dynamics 365 from the project side, enough to understand what the integration work is and why it takes the time it does.

  • Fluent with the work management, time tracking and financial tools a delivery team runs on, and used to keeping them reconciled.

Skills

  • Writes work definitions and acceptance criteria that a developer can build from without a conversation.

  • Delivers a firm message to an enterprise customer with the data behind it and stays in the room when it gets hard.

  • Builds trust with the customer and their team early, and keeps it through a firm conversation or a change order.

  • Reads budget burn and acts on a deviation before it becomes an overrun.

  • Holds several accounts at once without losing accuracy on any of them.

  • Writes updates a director or a customer sponsor can act on without a call.

  • Uses AI tools daily in their own work and checks what they produce before it reaches anyone else.

Who you are

You like owning a number and a customer relationship at the same time, and you’re comfortable being the person who says what a change will cost. You would rather define the work properly once. You have already worked with AI in delivery, you have an opinion on where it helps, and you want to be on a team that is putting it to work. You take ownership, build trust, drive innovation and succeed together, and you expect the same of the people around you.

Other information

  • Employment type: Full-time (40 hours/week)

  • Start date: Upon agreement

  • Location: Remote (U.S.), occasional travel for kickoffs and go-lives

  • Reports to: Director of Project Delivery, Commerce North America

  • Compensation: USD 80,000–100,000 annually, depending on experience and qualifications.

About Truvio

Truvio is a fast-growing SaaS company that combines established Microsoft Dynamics ISVs into one product portfolio built for Dynamics 365, helping customers get more value from their ERP investments. With our core values Take ownership, Build Trust, Drive innovation and Succeed together, we are about 450 employees worldwide across North America, Europe, Asia and Australia.

jobs.description:
Job Description

The Role


The HR Solutions Enablement team builds effective, scalable, and cohesive HR solutions that minimize redundancy and deliver seamless data and insights for a better end-user experience.


You’ll join a team that implements Workday and integrated third-party HR technology solutions to streamline operations and reduce friction. The team also provides Tier 2 support to business users. As the Sr. HR Technology Analyst for Hourly Compensation, you’ll design, configure, and maintain complex compensation processes across multiple countries and facilities, each with distinct requirements. This role combines consultative problem-solving, end-to-end execution, and the ability to influence without formal authority to deliver high-impact HR solutions.

Success in this role requires strong collaboration, consultation, and influence skills. You’ll partner with teams across the business to understand their challenges and implement optimal technology solutions—for example, translating hourly wage structures, step-progression rules, premiums, and allowances into robust, scalable Workday solutions that are accurate, compliant, and auditable.


The ideal candidate brings extensive hands-on experience with Workday Compensation configuration, working knowledge of adjacent Workday modules, and a passion for continuous improvement and solution design. You’ll serve as a Workday subject-matter expert and solution designer who improves system effectiveness, user experience, and operational scalability. Familiarity with emerging AI-powered tools and agents is valued, particularly where they can improve the end-user experience, Workday configurations and business processes.


Flexibility is important, as this role may occasionally require work outside standard hours to support global stakeholders and critical projects.


Key Responsibilities

  • Design and configure end-to-end Workday solutions for global hourly compensation, including compensation packages, grades, grade profiles, steps, eligibility rules, and plan assignments.
  • Configure and maintain complex hourly compensation components, including:
    • Base wage structures and wage scales
    • Premium pay structures and differential rules
    • Automatic step-progression schedules based on anniversaries, hours worked, or other business rules
    • Local allowances such as COLA, hazard, seniority, tool, transportation, and housing allowances
    • 13th- and 14th-month pay or similar country-specific components, where applicable
  • Translate requirements from local collective bargaining agreements (CBAs), country legislation, and compensation policies into clear, sustainable, and testable Workday solutions.
  • Design and maintain compensation eligibility rules using job profile, location, union or collective agreement, employee type, and other relevant attributes.
  • Lead or support projects to standardize and expand hourly compensation configuration, including discovery, design workshops, configuration, testing, deployment, and hypercare.
  • Partner with Payroll and Integration teams to ensure Workday compensation configurations support accurate downstream pay calculations and payroll processing.
  • Collaborate with Reporting and Analytics teams to ensure hourly compensation data supports downstream reporting, compliance, benchmarking, and decision-making.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve production issues related to hourly compensation, including eligibility errors, incorrect rates, step-progression defects, and missing allowances.
  • Execute and coordinate unit, integration, regression, and end-user testing; develop thorough test scenarios and maintain documentation describing solution configuration and expected outcomes.
  • Evaluate Workday releases and assess impacts to Compensation configuration, integrations, reporting, security, and business processes.
  • Apply Workday security and access controls, support data audits and control activities, and ensure configuration changes are documented, traceable and approved through established governance processes.
  • Validate, reconcile, and execute EIBs and other mass data updates in accordance with established data-quality and change-control standards.

Core Capabilities

  • Configuration and solution design: Independently turns complex hourly compensation problems into scalable Workday designs that balance standardization, usability, compliance and maintainability.
  • Stakeholder and consulting skills: Builds trust with HR, Compensation, Payroll, Labor Relations, and Technology stakeholders; clarifies requirements; and influences decisions with clear options and recommendations.
  • Execution discipline: Plans and delivers configuration work from design through testing, deployment, and hypercare with strong ownership and follow-through.
  • Continuous improvement and analysis: Uses data and root-cause analysis to diagnose issues and identify opportunities for process improvement, automation and better user experience.
  • Quality, governance, and controls: Maintains high standards for documentation, testing, change control, auditability, security and sustainable solution design.

Required Qualifications

  • You have 7+ years of progressive experience in HR technology, HRIS, compensation, or a related field, including at least 4 years of hands-on Workday configuration experience with a focus on Compensation.
  • You have advanced knowledge of hourly compensation practices, including wage scales, step progression, premiums, allowances, and related eligibility rules, and can model them cleanly in Workday.
  • You are fluent in Workday Compensation building blocks, including compensation packages, grades, grade profiles, steps, eligibility rules, and plan assignments, and understand how they work together.
  • You have built or supported Workday custom reports and calculated fields tied to compensation.
  • You are comfortable using Workday EIBs and mass-update patterns to safely move data at scale, including validation, reconciliation, and post-load review.
  • You can translate dense policy, legislation, and CBA language into clear, testable configurations and explain the logic to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • You have experience working across multiple countries or regions and navigating different regulatory and contractual environments to implement complex hourly compensation solutions.
  • You demonstrate professionalism, discretion and sound judgment when accessing sensitive employee information, using it only for legitimate business purposes and authorized work activities.
  • You bring strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with high attention to detail, data quality, and root-cause analysis.
  • You manage your work independently in a structured, change-managed environment and consistently deliver on your commitments.
  • You communicate clearly, in writing and in meetings, with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

What Will Give You An Edge

  • You hold a Workday Pro certification in Compensation or comparable advanced Workday training.
  • You have supported large hourly or manufacturing populations and understand the realities of plant and operations environments.
  • You have translated union or collective bargaining agreements into Workday designs for pay, step progression, premiums and allowances.
  • You have worked across additional Workday domains, such as Core HCM, Absence, Benefits, Recruiting, Talent, or Advanced Compensation, to design end-to-end HR solutions.
  • You understand Workday security fundamentals, including domain and business process security, role-based access, audit requirements, and internal controls.
  • You have led or co-led multi-country Workday initiatives or compensation optimizations and are comfortable owning portions of a global roadmap.
  • You have demonstrated the ability to identify and responsibly apply AI-powered tools or agents, such as copilots, chatbots, or automation frameworks, to improve the end-user experience, Workday configurations and business processes.

jobs.description:
Devenez chauffeur indépendant avec DriiveMe Partenaire

Accédez à des missions rémunérées de convoyage de véhicules partout en France, avec une organisation flexible et des frais de route pris en charge.

👉 Inscrivez-vous ici pour accéder aux missions :

DriiveMe est la plateforme leader européen du convoyage de véhicules. Chaque mois, plus de 20 000 missions rémunérées sont proposées à notre communauté de chauffeurs et convoyeurs indépendants partout en France.

Les grands acteurs de l’automobile font confiance à DriiveMe pour déplacer leurs véhicules : Stellantis, Aramisauto, Ayvens, Tesla, Volkswagen, Hertz, Avis, Europcar, et bien d’autres.

Partout en France, des centaines de sociétés ont besoin de déplacer des véhicules d’un point A à un point B. Elles publient chaque jour leurs besoins sur DriiveMe afin de proposer ces missions à la communauté DriiveMe Partenaire.

En quoi consiste une mission DriiveMe ?

C’est simple : en tant que chauffeur indépendant, vous conduisez un véhicule d’un point A vers un point B. Voici comment ça fonctionne :

  1. Vous créez votre compte sur

  2. Vous accédez aux missions disponibles dans votre région.

  3. Vous consultez le trajet, la rémunération et les conditions de chaque mission.

  4. Vous réservez en quelques clics les missions que vous souhaitez réaliser.

  5. Le jour de la mission, vous récupérez le véhicule au point de départ et le livrez au point d’arrivée.

  6. Une fois la mission terminée et validée, vous recevez votre paiement automatiquement sous 10 jours.

Pourquoi devenir chauffeur indépendant avec DriiveMe Partenaire ?

  • Complément de revenus : chaque mission est rémunérée, avec un prix connu à l’avance.

  • Organisation flexible : vous choisissez librement les missions que vous souhaitez effectuer.

  • Frais de route pris en charge : carburant et péages sont remboursés selon les conditions de la mission.

  • Plateforme simple et intuitive : consultation, réservation et suivi des missions en ligne.

  • Missions partout en France : de nouvelles opportunités sont publiées chaque jour.

Combien suis-je rémunéré ?

Votre chiffre d'affaires dépend du nombre de missions que vous choisissez de réaliser.

Chaque mission dispose d’une rémunération spécifique, définie selon le trajet, le nombre de kilomètres et la complexité du transport.

Avant de réserver une mission, vous connaissez les informations essentielles : lieu de départ, lieu d’arrivée, rémunération et conditions de prise en charge. Vous êtes libre de réserver uniquement les missions qui vous conviennent.

Profil recherché

Pour rejoindre DriiveMe Partenaire, vous devez idéalement :
